observations.observed: Markets pay-per-result APIs with exact price, verifiable delivery and receipts across a large governed catalogue.
observations.implication: James must not claim pay-per-result or verifiable delivery alone as differentiation.

observations.observed: Indexes current availability, published prices and live 402 quote checks at large scale and explicitly discusses workflow cost including retries.
observations.implication: Discovery, quote validation, price comparison and generic retry-aware workflow costing are not sufficient moat.

observations.observed: Offers 578 tools, spend caps and a web-search route at USD 0.02/call.
observations.implication: Spend caps and raw per-call pricing are baseline controls, not differentiation.

observations.observed: Structured search is directly purchasable over x402; basic/advanced search pricing is approximately USD 0.01-0.02 depending on route/depth.
observations.implication: Tavily remains a suitable paid benchmark candidate once signer controls pass.

surviving_wedge: Exact-task, request-equivalent, post-payment measurement of settled spend plus retries plus deterministic acceptance PASS/FAIL plus latency, converted into effective cost per acceptable result and backed by reproducible evidence.
positioning_constraints: Do not claim generic x402 discovery as differentiation.
Do not claim price comparison as differentiation.
Do not claim spend caps as differentiation.
Do not claim pay-per-result or delivery receipts alone as differentiation.
Do not claim superiority until real paid benchmark evidence demonstrates it.
kill_or_reposition_trigger: If a credible competitor exposes request-equivalent cross-provider benchmarks with deterministic task acceptance, observed paid retries, settled cost and effective cost per acceptable result, reassess the wedge before further commercial investment.
